conventions.convention: The underlying manifold is nonempty, compact, smooth, three-dimensional and without boundary. The conformal metric and symmetric TT covariant two-tensor are smooth, τ is constant, and φ is smooth and strictly positive. Vacuum means zero stress-energy and Λ=0.
Curvature is R(X,Y)Z=D_XD_YZ−D_YD_XZ−D_[X,Y]Z; Ric(m)_ij=R[m]^k_ikj. The scalar Laplacian is the metric trace of the Hessian, with negative Fourier symbol on nonconstant torus characters.
The embedded interpretation uses K(X,Y)=g(∇_X n,Y) for the future unit normal. The residuals are H=R(h)+(tr_h K)^2−|K|_h^2 and M=div_h K−d(tr_h K).
The conformal ansatz weights the covariant TT tensor: h=φ^4 h̃ and K=φ^−2 σ̃+(τ/3)h. TT means zero h̃-trace and zero h̃-divergence.

Countable Choice is assumed for the Fourier Sobolev suppliers and embedded Lorentzian interpretation; the abstract conformal tensor identities and constant-root calculation do not themselves spend a choice principle.
The Fourier inverse uses dimensionless coordinates modulo 2π, metric h̃=L_*^2 Σ_i(dx^i)^2 with L_*>0, normalized probability measure, characters exp(ik·x), k∈Z^3, and integer Sobolev orders s≥2.
Uniqueness of the positive twelfth-root solution is asserted only among positive constant conformal factors, under R̃=0, A=|σ̃|²>0 and τ≠0.
Coercivity in the zero-mode example means a lower bound by c₀ times the full derivative H¹ norm squared for every smooth real function, with c₀>0; constants are included.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated smooth compact boundaryless three-manifold, smooth Riemannian h̃, smooth covariant TT tensor σ̃, constant τ and positive smooth φ, define h=φ^4 h̃, K=φ^−2 σ̃+(τ/3)h and the Hamiltonian and momentum residuals H=R(h)+(tr_h K)^2−|K|_h^2 and M=div_h K−d(tr_h K).
For the defined vacuum conformal data, tr_h K=τ, M(h,K)=0, and H(h,K)=0 if and only if −8Δ̃φ+R̃φ−|σ̃|²φ^−7+(2/3)τ²φ^5=0.
For vacuum conformal data with R̃=0, constant A=|σ̃|²>0 and constant τ≠0, the Lichnerowicz equation has exactly one positive constant solution, φ₀=(3A/(2τ²))^(1/12).

At the stated flat-torus constant solution, the directional linearization is A v=−8Δ̃v+cv, where c=7Aφ₀^−8+(10/3)τ²φ₀^4>0. It is strictly positive on nonzero smooth real functions and a bounded bijection H^(s+2)→H^s for every integer s≥2, with inverse Fourier multiplier (8L_*^−2|k|²+c)^−1 and the stated two-derivative estimate.
